event: The Mk.V Sentinel opens its Flux eyes, and a fourth construct slot lights in Callum's interface.
A meter tall on suspension-strut legs, with an engine-block torso: ugly, and his best work.
Diagnostics: combat, slot 4 of 4, Overgrowth Level 10-15, 55 Flux an hour, five lines loaded.
Two days went into those lines: basic loop, heavy strike under 50%, retreat at 30% integrity.
"Not elegant. But functional," he says aloud, and Pip flickers.
The Sentinel tags him as no threat and scans the warehouse with jerky turns of its head.
He slots its last Flux Capacitor and says "Go"; it walks south toward the Overgrowth.
At the Overgrowth boundary he watches the Sentinel through Loop Sight, notebook open.
Four minutes in, two vine constrictors, Level 10 and 11, coil at an oak; the Sentinel engages.
It sidesteps clumsily and hits for about 15 a strike; a kill takes some forty seconds.
A constrictor cracks its caliper arm to 94% integrity; it keeps swinging and kills it.
The second takes thirty-eight seconds, integrity 87%. Not elegant. Functional.
He logs the kills: about 24 Essence, scrap relay nominal, the heavy-strike branch untested.
At two or three kills a cycle, he works out 847 Essence a day from the Sentinel alone.
His daily projection jumps from about 1,555 to 2,402 Essence, up 54.5%.
Level 13 in 1.2 days, 14 in 3.7, 15 in 7.1. Something warm and quiet moves in his chest.
He leans on a broken wall watching the Sentinel's iron bar flash in the haze. "Yeah. I know."
Fourteen hours on, at 3:17 AM on his warehouse cot, the level-up arrives: 12 to 13.

changes.note: Level 12 to 13 as the Mk.V's kills push him over the threshold

event: Warmth floods him; his vision sharpens, and a three-day headache vanishes.
Level 11 to 12 took nine days; the Mk.V cut 12 to 13 to under a day and a half.
He puts two points in Intelligence, to 51, and two in Wisdom, to 54.
One point into Willpower, to 29, lifts his session duration from 9.6 to 9.8 hours.
His window: Loopweaver Level 13, Prestige 0, Script Complexity 30.5, Idle Yield 2.08x.
He holds five skill points; Script Engine 2 costs four and fifteen Chrono Dust. Not yet.
Still splitting resources at 3:22 AM, he tells himself sleep is a valid optimization.
The loop runs: Sentinel in the Overgrowth, Grinder in the Flats, Collector and Refinery at work.
Late that afternoon he walks out to check a 2.3% overnight dip in the Sentinel's efficiency.
Skirting the patrol edge, he hears fast metal on flesh and the coughing snarl of spore wolves.
His Level 3 Danger Sense tingles: violence within fifty meters. He creeps closer to assess.
From a clearing's edge he sees six spore wolves, Level 11 to 14, attacking in pack formation.
At their centre, killing them, is the Sword Saint from the Grind Pits.
Blood streaks her left arm; she fights like someone fencing since nine, now killing monsters.
Riposte opens a wolf from jaw to shoulder; Dash carries her between two flankers.
Her Read Opponent stacks climb to six in his Loop Sight: an eighteen percent damage bonus.
The sixth wolf hits her from behind; her HP drops to 80%, then 74% as its spores tick.
He reckons she wins at about 60% HP, but the flanker will strike again, and might crit.
Redirecting the Sentinel will cost ninety seconds and about 16 Essence. It doesn't matter.
Without deciding, he drags the Mk.V's patrol marker onto the sixth wolf.
The Sentinel crashes out of the undergrowth like a filing cabinet thrown down a staircase.
The wolf turns on it and dodges easily; the construct only has to keep it busy.
In eight seconds the Sword Saint kills the rest of the pack with Riposte, Dash and Deathmark.
She kills the sixth wolf with one clean thrust through its skull.
The clearing goes still; the Sentinel finds no target and trundles back to its patrol.
She looks past the construct to Callum, standing in full view with his notebook.
She walks over, saber in hand, blood on her forearm, and asks if the construct is his.
"It fights like a drunk toddler." It killed the wolf, he says; it occupied it, she says.
It bought her eight seconds, he says; she looks at him properly and reads his level: 13.
"The construct runs the patrol. I optimize the construct," he explains.
She has never seen his class icon. "Loopweaver," he says; she has never heard of it.
"I'm Mira. Vasquez," she offers, handle first. "Callum Voss." "The guy in the warehouse."
People talk, she says, about the weirdo in the Foundry District running constructs all night.
Then she frowns at her hands: her attack speed and cooldowns have shifted. "What are you doing?"
His Optimization Aura shows faint new text: proximity resonance, bleed radius 3m, effect unknown.
"I don't know," he says: the most honest thing he has said in months.
"You have an aura." It is supposed to be self-only, he says. "Well, it's not."
She asks if he has ever stood near another player with it running. "No. I have not."
Her speed is up two or three percent, cooldowns shorter, from someone eleven levels below her.
At his "I agree" she laughs, sharp and surprised, and her face goes younger for half a second.
Why send the construct? "It seemed correct." He talks like a System notification, she says.
"I'm going to come back," Mira says; she has questions about his constructs and his aura.
It fights like a drunk toddler, she says, but it showed up when it mattered. Then she is gone.
His heart is racing; the aura's self-only label, he notes, may be only a threshold.
He writes four questions, and underlines three times whether the Substrate has known.
Walking back forty minutes, he catches himself evaluating Mira like a subroutine.
The night air is cold, and for the first time in a long while he does not want to be invisible.
She said she would come back. It fits no spreadsheet, and it warms his chest.
He tells Pip she will have questions he can't answer, and worse, ones he can.
In the warehouse all four slots run, and Essence comes in at the new rate.
The Enhancement Construct still sits at 75%, waiting for Bloom Crystal he can't afford yet.
For the first time in four months he falls asleep thinking of something other than the curve.
